articles.title: Middleton Residents Call for Reconsideration of Parking Restrictions on Grimshaw Lane
articles.excerpt: Residents on Grimshaw Lane in Middleton are urging local councillors to rethink proposed parking restrictions aimed at improving safety and traffic flow. The plans will be discussed at the Middleton Township Committee meeting on 14 September 2026.
articles.content_html:
Residents on Grimshaw Lane in Middleton are urging local councillors to reconsider proposed parking restrictions that could significantly affect parking outside their homes. The Middleton Township Committee is set to discuss objections to these plans during its meeting on Thursday, 14 September 2026.

The proposed restrictions come in response to ongoing issues with speeding, serious accidents—including a fatality—and inconsiderate parking that has disrupted bus services in the area. A report from Rochdale Council's Highways department highlights that the north-western section of Grimshaw Lane, between Greengate and Townley Street, has been identified as a location with poor bus service reliability due to congestion and obstructive parking.

To address these concerns, the council's proposal includes the installation of new footway build-outs to narrow pedestrian crossing widths at several junctions, as well as the addition of three new pedestrian refuge islands to facilitate safer crossings. Furthermore, the plans involve extending bus stop bays and introducing double yellow lines along much of the northern side of Grimshaw Lane, particularly from Saxon Street to Sedgley Street, to ensure the safe passage of vehicles, including refuse collection and HGVs servicing local businesses.

The outcome of the committee meeting will determine whether the proposed parking restrictions will be implemented or if further adjustments will be made to accommodate residents' concerns. Local residents are encouraged to attend the meeting to voice their opinions on the matter.

articles.title: Mother Hubbard Opens in Middleton, Attracting Large Crowds and Boosting Local Trade
articles.excerpt: Mother Hubbard has opened a new branch in Middleton Shopping Centre, offering 45p fish and chips to the first 1,000 customers, boosting local fish and chip sales including at the nearby Middleton Fish Bar.
articles.content_html:
A new fish and chip shop, Mother Hubbard, opened its doors in Middleton Shopping Centre on Saturday, 12 September 2026, offering a special promotion of 45p fish and chips for the first 1,000 customers. This opening drew significant crowds, with queues stretching back to the bus station as locals flocked to sample the menu.

Among the first customers was Colin Thompson, who praised the quality of the food and the hard work of the staff on social media. Other patrons echoed his sentiments, expressing excitement about the new addition to the local dining scene. Misa Ila commented on Facebook, stating, "Great venue, good luck to them. The Rochdale one is mint," while Pat Keogh added, "Well done and good luck. Glad Middleton is getting sorted now, it’s about time."

The opening of Mother Hubbard coincided with a busy day for the nearby Middleton Fish Bar, which reported selling out of its stock and closing early at 2.30pm due to high demand. Owners Paul and Caroline High thanked their customers for their support, highlighting the strong community response to both establishments.

The successful launch of Mother Hubbard and the bustling trade at Middleton Fish Bar suggest a growing appetite for fish and chips in the area, which may encourage further investment in local dining options. Residents can expect a vibrant fish and chip scene in Middleton as both businesses continue to serve the community.

articles.title: £12m plan aims to bring Storage World Middleton site back to life after devastating fire
articles.excerpt: A £12m rebirth bid has been launched for the Storage World site in Middleton, more than a year after a devastating fire destroyed the Old Hall Street facility.
articles.content_html:
A £12m bid to bring the Storage World site in Middleton back to life has been launched, marking a major potential investment in an important part of the town centre following last year's devastating fire.

The proposals concern the Storage World site on Old Hall Street, next to Middleton Arena. The former storage facility was badly damaged by a major blaze in June 2025, which burned for several days and led to demolition of the building. No injuries were reported, although customers and businesses suffered significant losses.

Place North West has reported that Storage World has now launched a £12m rebirth bid for the site. The move comes as regeneration work and planning for the wider Middleton town centre area continues.

Official Rochdale Development Agency updates show that the council and RDA have remained in discussions with Storage World since the fire. In June, the RDA said it was working with stakeholders to develop key principles for the area, including the potential to deliver improvements to Middleton Arena and create a new public space. It also confirmed that discussions with Storage World were continuing with input from Rochdale Borough Council's planning team.

The site is particularly significant because of its position beside Middleton Arena and within an area being considered as part of wider plans for the future of Middleton town centre. Earlier council reports said the outcomes of discussions over Storage World and the arena would feed into wider masterplanning work.

Before the fire, Storage World operated a large self-storage and workspace facility from Old Hall Street. The Middleton operation had previously expanded as demand grew, with the company providing traditional storage alongside space used by small and online businesses.

The 2025 blaze had a substantial impact on customers. Fire crews worked for days at the scene and parts of the building were demolished while firefighting operations were still under way to allow crews safe access. Storage World said at the time that its team was devastated by the impact on customers and the wider community.

The latest £12m proposal therefore represents a potentially significant next chapter for a prominent town-centre site and comes at a time when Middleton is the subject of wider regeneration and masterplanning proposals.

Rochdale Daily will update this story as further planning documents and details of the proposed redevelopment become publicly available.

articles.title: Middleton protest planned as organiser sets out bail conditions ahead of event
articles.excerpt: A protest is planned in Middleton Gardens on 8 August, with organiser Jamie Thomason outlining his intended arrangements and referring to bail conditions while police are expected to oversee the event.
articles.content_html:
A public protest is due to take place in Middleton Gardens on Saturday, 8 August, with organiser Jamie Thomason stating he intends to comply with his bail conditions while addressing supporters before leaving the area. According to a statement published on social media, Greater Manchester Police will have officers present during the event, with police liaison officers said to be aware of the arrangements.

In his announcement, Thomason said he would be joined by several guest speakers from across the UK, including Ashlea Simon of All for England, Dorothy Jones and Pag Billy UK, with additional speakers yet to be confirmed. He described his planned speech as being based on information which he says can be verified through publicly available sources and encouraged supporters to attend the demonstration.

Thomason also referred to his current bail conditions, stating that he is prohibited from congregating with more than ten people. He asked supporters not to approach him in groups, saying he had agreed with Greater Manchester Police that he would attend, deliver his speech and leave Middleton immediately afterwards. He also stated that he would give his speech from a distance and would not become involved in any confrontation because he did not intend to breach his bail conditions.

Rochdale Daily has not independently verified the specific bail conditions referred to in Thomason's post, and reports them only as claims made by the organiser himself.

The right to peaceful protest is protected in UK law under Article 11 of the European Convention on Human Rights, although that right is subject to restrictions where they are lawful, necessary and proportionate. Police have powers under the Public Order Act 1986, as amended by more recent legislation including the Public Order Act 2023, to impose conditions on public assemblies where they reasonably believe serious public disorder, serious disruption, intimidation or damage may occur. Participants are expected to comply with any lawful conditions imposed.

Greater Manchester Police has previously stated that its role at public demonstrations is to facilitate peaceful and lawful protest while taking action where criminal offences are committed or where public safety is at risk. Depending on the circumstances, officers may deploy protest liaison teams, public order officers or other resources to manage events and minimise disruption to the wider community.

The planned demonstration is likely to attract differing opinions from residents. Supporters say the event is intended to raise awareness of issues they believe are affecting communities across the country, while others are expected to disagree with both the organisers and the views expressed. Peaceful disagreement and lawful protest are protected rights, provided they remain within the limits of the law.

Anyone travelling through Middleton town centre on Saturday should be aware that there may be an increased police presence around Middleton Gardens while the demonstration takes place. At the time of publication, no official road closures, dispersal orders or protest conditions had been publicly announced.

Rochdale Daily has contacted Greater Manchester Police for comment to confirm the policing arrangements for the event, including whether officers will be deployed, whether any conditions have been imposed under public order legislation, and whether any road closures, dispersal powers or other measures are anticipated. This article will be updated if and when a response is received.
